vocabulary.translation: 他在演讲中猛烈抨击了那些批评者。

vocabulary.entry: loathe /ləʊð/ v. 厌恶；憎恶
vocabulary.example: She loathes the sound of nails scratching a blackboard.
vocabulary.translation: 她极其厌恶指甲刮擦黑板的声音。

vocabulary.entry: panic /ˈpænɪk/ v. （使）恐慌；惊慌
vocabulary.example: The sound of the alarm made everyone panic.
vocabulary.translation: 警报声让所有人都惊慌失措。

vocabulary.entry: activate /ˈæktɪveɪt/ v. 激活；触发
vocabulary.example: The alarm activates automatically when a door opens.
vocabulary.translation: 只要有一扇门打开，警报就会自动激活。

sentences.english: There are some sounds most of us acknowledge are irritating – the crunching of crisps, the humming of the air conditioning or a screaming baby.
sentences.chinese: 我们大多数人都认同，有些声音确实很刺耳——比如咀嚼薯片的嘎吱声、空调的嗡嗡声，或是婴儿的哭闹声。

sentences.english: These noises, for many people, act as a mere inconvenience that can distract us from the task at hand.
sentences.chinese: 对很多人来说，这些噪音只是小麻烦，会让我们分心，无法专注于手头的事情。

sentences.english: However, there are some amongst us who have a much more severe response to these noises.
sentences.chinese: 但有些人对这类声音的反应要剧烈得多。

sentences.english: The question we ask today is: has a noise ever made you feel so angry that you could explode with rage?
sentences.chinese: 今天我们要探讨的问题是：你是否曾因为某个声音而愤怒到近乎抓狂？

sentences.english: If the answer is yes, you may be suffering from misophonia.
sentences.chinese: 如果答案是肯定的，那你可能患上了恐音症。

sentences.english: The word ‘misophonia’ literally means ‘a hatred of sound’ and is sometimes called Selective Sound Sensitivity Syndrome.
sentences.chinese: “恐音症”这个词的字面意思就是“对声音的厌恶”，它有时也被称为选择性声音敏感综合征。

sentences.english: There are some experts who doubt the existence of the condition. However, for those who claim to suffer from it, the experience can be traumatic.
sentences.chinese: 有些专家怀疑这种病症是否真的存在，但对那些自称患有恐音症的人来说，这种体验是极具创伤性的。

sentences.english: Certain sounds trigger intense emotional or psychological responses that may seem over the top compared with a non-sufferer’s complaints.
sentences.chinese: 某些特定声音会引发他们强烈的情绪或心理反应，相较于非患者的不满，这种反应显得有些过分夸张。

sentences.english: The sound of a loved one chewing their food could trigger a sufferer’s anxiety levels, or cause them to panic.
sentences.chinese: 挚爱之人咀嚼食物的声音，都可能让恐音症患者的焦虑感飙升，甚至引发恐慌。

sentences.english: It may even activate their fight-or-flight reflexes, making them want to flee.
sentences.chinese: 这种声音甚至会激活他们的“战斗或逃跑”本能，让他们想要立刻逃离。

sentences.english: In extreme cases, that feeling of panic may result in intense bouts of fury and end up with sufferers going berserk.
sentences.chinese: 在极端情况下，这种恐慌感会转化为一阵阵暴怒，最终导致患者情绪失控、行为失常。

sentences.english: Sadly, there’s no known cure.
sentences.chinese: 遗憾的是，目前恐音症尚无方法可以治疗。

sentences.english: Tinnitus retraining therapy, which helps people tolerate noises, may aid sufferers, while cognitive behavioural therapy and counselling could also help people manage the condition.
sentences.chinese: 能帮助人们耐受噪音的耳鸣再训练疗法或许能为患者提供帮助，认知行为疗法和心理咨询也有助于患者控制病情。

sentences.english: According to James Cartreine, a clinical psychiatrist, the condition can lead to isolation.
sentences.chinese: 临床精神病学家詹姆斯·卡特赖恩表示，恐音症可能会导致患者与世隔绝。

sentences.english: Sufferers use coping strategies that include avoiding places with lots of noises, like restaurants, or moving away when they feel like lashing out at someone due to their breathing.
sentences.chinese: 患者会采取各种应对策略，比如避开餐厅这类噪音密集的场所，或是当别人的呼吸声让他们忍不住想要发作时，选择立刻走开。

sentences.english: So, the next time you see someone fly into a rage because of a sound that is driving them crazy, it may be due to a difficult condition they are trying to manage, and not just because they loathe a certain sound.
sentences.chinese: 所以下次当你看到有人因为某个声音而勃然大怒、几近崩溃时，这可能并非因为他们单纯讨厌那种声音，而是因为他们正在艰难地应对一种病症。

title: The future of cinema
paragraphs: Are you a moviegoer? If, like me, you’re a fan of film, then there’s no better place to watch something than on the big screen at the cinema. You enter the dark auditorium and take your seat, ready to be entertained. But while you engross yourself in some movie magic, many others are now getting their film fix at home.

Over the last few years, cinemas have seen a resurgence. Customers have been enticed by comfortable seats, and lots of choice of things to watch. Multiplexes in particular can screen up to twenty films at the same time, catering for all different tastes. In addition, 3D and even 4D movies can give the audience an extra immersive experience. So, what’s not to like about a trip to the cinema?

One answer to that question is convenience. Rather than going out, it’s so much easier to stay in and watch a romcom or action movie on a high-definition TV screen via a streaming service such as Netflix or Amazon Prime. There’s plenty of choice, and it’s relatively cheap as well. But, personally, I find there are too many distractions, and watching at home is not such an event. I miss the trailers too!

But the coronavirus pandemic has put the future of cinemas under the spotlight. Some have had to close because of reduced ticket sales. And in the UK, it’s brought about a surge in TV watching and online streaming, according to media watchdog, Ofcom. It also found that half of UK adults will keep and continue using their new streaming subscriptions.

This isn’t great news for cinemas. They rely on the release of a big blockbuster to bring the crowds back, but the launch of new films, such as James Bond: No Time To Die, are being delayed. And Disney has released its $200m blockbuster, Mulan, online instead of in movie theatres. But John Fithian, from the National Association of Theatre Owners, told Variety magazine: “This idea of waiting out the pandemic to make your movies more profitable doesn’t make sense to me. There won’t be as much of an industry left to play your movies in if you do that.”

vocabulary.entry: moviegoer /ˈmuːviɡəʊə/ n. 影迷；常看电影的人
vocabulary.example: The cinema attracts a large number of moviegoers at weekends.
vocabulary.translation: 这家电影院周末吸引了大批影迷。

vocabulary.entry: big screen /bɪɡ skriːn/ n. （电影院的）大屏幕
vocabulary.example: Watching a film on the big screen is quite different from on TV.
vocabulary.translation: 在大屏幕上看电影和在电视上看感觉很不一样。

vocabulary.entry: auditorium /ˌɔːdɪˈtɔːriəm/ n. （电影院的）放映厅
vocabulary.example: The auditorium was packed with people waiting for the film to start.
vocabulary.translation: 放映厅里坐满了等待电影开场的人。

vocabulary.entry: engross oneself in /ɪnˈɡrəʊs wʌnˈself ɪn/ 沉浸于；全神贯注于
vocabulary.example: She engrossed herself in the novel and forgot about the time.
vocabulary.translation: 她沉浸在小说里，忘记了时间。

vocabulary.entry: movie magic /ˈmuːvi ˈmædʒɪk/ n. 电影的奇幻魅力
vocabulary.example: The director used special effects to create the movie magic on screen.
vocabulary.translation: 导演运用特效在银幕上营造出了电影的奇幻魅力。

vocabulary.entry: film fix /fɪlm fɪks/ n. 电影瘾；观影的满足感
vocabulary.example: He gets his film fix by streaming movies every weekend.
vocabulary.translation: 他每周末都靠流媒体看电影来满足自己的观影瘾。

vocabulary.entry: resurgence /rɪˈneɪsns/ n. 复苏；复兴
vocabulary.example: There has been a resurgence of interest in traditional crafts recently.
vocabulary.translation: 近来人们对传统手工艺的兴趣再度兴起。

vocabulary.entry: entice /ɪnˈtaɪs/ v. 吸引；诱惑
vocabulary.example: The store enticed customers with special discounts.
vocabulary.translation: 这家商店用特别折扣吸引顾客。

vocabulary.entry: multiplex /ˈmʌltɪpleks/ n. 多厅影院
vocabulary.example: The new multiplex in the city centre has 12 screens.
vocabulary.translation: 市中心那家新的多厅影院有12个放映厅。

vocabulary.entry: cater for /ˈkeɪtə fɔː/ 满足……的需求；迎合
vocabulary.example: The restaurant caters for both vegetarian and non-vegetarian customers.
vocabulary.translation: 这家餐厅既满足素食者也满足非素食者的需求。

vocabulary.entry: immersive experience /ɪˈmɜːsɪv ɪkˈspɪəriəns/ n. 沉浸式体验
vocabulary.example: The VR game offers an immersive experience for players.
vocabulary.translation: 这款虚拟现实游戏为玩家带来沉浸式体验。

vocabulary.entry: convenience /kənˈviːniəns/ n. 便利性；方便
vocabulary.example: Online shopping is popular because of its convenience.
vocabulary.translation: 网购因其便利性而深受欢迎。

vocabulary.entry: romcom /ˈrɒmkɒm/ n. 浪漫喜剧片
vocabulary.example: We watched a light-hearted romcom last night.
vocabulary.translation: 我们昨晚看了一部轻松的浪漫喜剧片。

vocabulary.entry: action movie /ˈækʃn ˈmuːvi/ n. 动作片
vocabulary.example: He is a big fan of action movies starring Jackie Chan.
vocabulary.translation: 他是成龙主演的动作片的铁杆粉丝。

vocabulary.entry: high-definition /ˌhaɪ ˌdefɪˈnɪʃn/ adj. 高清的
vocabulary.example: We bought a high-definition TV for watching movies at home.
vocabulary.translation: 我们买了一台高清电视，方便在家看电影。

vocabulary.entry: streaming service /ˈstriːmɪŋ ˈsɜːvɪs/ n. 流媒体服务
vocabulary.example: Many people subscribe to at least one streaming service now.
vocabulary.translation: 现在很多人至少订阅了一项流媒体服务。

vocabulary.entry: distraction /dɪˈstrækʃn/ n. 使人分心的事物
vocabulary.example: The noise from the street is a distraction when I'm working.
vocabulary.translation: 街上的噪音在我工作时会让我分心。

vocabulary.entry: put under the spotlight /pʊt ˈʌndə ðə ˈspɒtlaɪt/ 使成为焦点；受到关注
vocabulary.example: The environmental problem has been put under the spotlight recently.
vocabulary.translation: 近来环境问题成为了关注焦点。

vocabulary.entry: ticket sale /ˈtɪkɪt seɪl/ n. 票房销售
vocabulary.example: Ticket sales for the new film have broken all records.
vocabulary.translation: 这部新片的票房销售额打破了所有纪录。

vocabulary.entry: surge /sɜːdʒ/ n. 激增；猛增
vocabulary.example: There has been a surge in demand for face masks during the pandemic.
vocabulary.translation: 疫情期间，口罩的需求量激增。

vocabulary.entry: blockbuster /ˈblɒkbʌstə/ n. 重磅大片；轰动一时的影片
vocabulary.example: The new superhero movie is expected to be a summer blockbuster.
vocabulary.translation: 这部新的超级英雄电影有望成为暑期档重磅大片。

vocabulary.entry: delay /dɪˈleɪ/ v. 推迟；延期
vocabulary.example: The company decided to delay the launch of its new product.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司决定推迟其新产品的上市时间。

sentences.english: Are you a moviegoer?
sentences.chinese: 你是一名影迷吗？

sentences.english: If, like me, you’re a fan of film, then there’s no better place to watch something than on the big screen at the cinema.
sentences.chinese: 如果你和我一样热爱电影，那么没有什么地方比电影院的大屏幕更适合观影了。

sentences.english: You enter the dark auditorium and take your seat, ready to be entertained.
sentences.chinese: 你走进昏暗的放映厅，落座之后，便准备好开启一场视听盛宴。

sentences.english: But while you engross yourself in some movie magic, many others are now getting their film fix at home.
sentences.chinese: 但就在你沉浸于电影的奇幻魅力时，如今有许多人选择在家就能过足电影瘾。

sentences.english: Over the last few years, cinemas have seen a resurgence.
sentences.chinese: 在过去几年里，电影院行业迎来了复苏。

sentences.english: Customers have been enticed by comfortable seats, and lots of choice of things to watch.
sentences.chinese: 舒适的座椅以及丰富多样的影片选择，吸引了不少观众前来。

sentences.english: Multiplexes in particular can screen up to twenty films at the same time, catering for all different tastes.
sentences.chinese: 尤其是多厅影院，能够同时放映多达二十部影片，满足不同观众的口味。

sentences.english: In addition, 3D and even 4D movies can give the audience an extra immersive experience.
sentences.chinese: 此外，3D甚至4D电影还能为观众带来更具沉浸感的体验。

sentences.english: So, what’s not to like about a trip to the cinema?
sentences.chinese: 如此说来，去电影院观影还有什么让人不满意的地方呢？

sentences.english: One answer to that question is convenience.
sentences.chinese: 这个问题的答案之一就是便利性。

sentences.english: Rather than going out, it’s so much easier to stay in and watch a romcom or action movie on a high-definition TV screen via a streaming service such as Netflix or Amazon Prime.
sentences.chinese: 比起出门，待在家里通过网飞或亚马逊Prime这类流媒体平台，在高清电视屏幕上看一部浪漫喜剧或动作片要轻松得多。

sentences.english: There’s plenty of choice, and it’s relatively cheap as well.
sentences.chinese: 影片选择十分丰富，价格也相对实惠。

sentences.english: But, personally, I find there are too many distractions, and watching at home is not such an event.
sentences.chinese: 但就我个人而言，我觉得在家观影干扰太多，和影院观影完全不是一回事。

sentences.english: I miss the trailers too!
sentences.chinese: 我还很想念电影预告片呢！

sentences.english: But the coronavirus pandemic has put the future of cinemas under the spotlight.
sentences.chinese: 但新冠疫情的爆发让电影院的未来被推上了风口浪尖。

sentences.english: Some have had to close because of reduced ticket sales.
sentences.chinese: 部分影院因票房收入下滑而不得不关门歇业。

sentences.english: And in the UK, it’s brought about a surge in TV watching and online streaming, according to media watchdog, Ofcom.
sentences.chinese: 英国媒体监管机构英国通信管理局表示，疫情还使得英国的电视观看量和在线流媒体播放量大幅飙升。

sentences.english: It also found that half of UK adults will keep and continue using their new streaming subscriptions.

title: Cold-water swimming
paragraphs: We all know about the health benefits of swimming. It offers a great workout for the body – it builds endurance, muscle strength and cardiovascular fitness. If you don’t mind getting wet, it can be fun too. But who would enjoy swimming in water that’s ice cold? Well, many people are taking the plunge, based on evidence that it can actually be good for us.

Cold-water swimming – sometimes called wild swimming – involves swimming in natural areas including ponds, rivers and the sea. Jumping in gives a short sharp shock to the body, but many participants say they get used to it. A cold dip might wake you up, but research has found it can have much bigger benefits than that for your body and mind. As well as being good exercise, spending time outdoors and by water improves wellbeing.

There is much evidence, mostly anecdotal, that suggests cold-water swimming has cured certain health conditions. One man who suffered constant pain after surgery claimed he was cured by taking a plunge in cold open water. And another swimmer, Sandria Simons, told the BBC “the immersion of your body in cold, salt water, just feeling like you’re at one with nature if you like, just feels amazing.” But what is it that people are gaining from this chilly experience? Doctors say getting into cold water evokes a stress response, but the more you do it, your reaction to stress is reduced. It’s also thought to have a strong anti-inflammatory effect. But there are bigger benefits to this stress-reducing exercise. Some experts believe cold-water swimming helps ‘cross-adaptation’, where one form of stress prepares the body for another. For example, it also helps reduce the stress of exercising at high altitude.
So, if you’re convinced that this is for you, take advice: approach it with caution, swim with a friend, and maybe start in the summer, when the water temperatures are higher!

title: Living under the sea
paragraphs: There are people living in almost every corner of our crowded planet. From the tops of mountains to deep underground, we’ve always been able to find habitable places to make a home. But with space at a premium, we’ve started to look even deeper for somewhere to live.

Throughout history, people have been fascinated by the idea of living underwater. More recently, the effects of human activity on the land have led some to look to the oceans for natural resources. Oceanographers and architects have looked at designing vessels, labs and underwater habitats to enable people to live and work in a submerged world. But, while dreams of an aquatic city have remained a fantasy, how close are we to making our home on the seabed a reality?

The pioneer of undersea living was Ian Koblick, sometimes described as an ‘aquanaut’. He claimed technology already existed to create underwater colonies supporting up to a hundred people. He even opened La Chalupa, once the largest and most advanced underwater habitat and research facility in the world.

A more recent and ambitious design for an underwater city is Ocean Spiral. Designed by the Japanese Shimizu Corporation, it’s a huge transparent globe attached to the seabed. It’s got a tower running through it to the surface, providing space for homes, offices and even an amusement park for five thousand residents. Masaki Takeuchi from the company told the BBC: “Our idea is to connect the sea surface and the deep sea vertically, and that way we believe that we can utilise the capability of the deep sea.”

Of course, there are engineering challenges in constructing an oceanic metropolis. And living underwater would have major effects on the human body, especially as there is an increase in atmospheric pressure which could lead to the bends. So, maybe it’s too soon to be packing our bags and setting up a new life three thousand metres under the sea!

sentences.english: Masaki Takeuchi from the company told the BBC: “Our idea is to connect the sea surface and the deep sea vertically, and that way we believe that we can utilise the capability of the deep sea.”
sentences.chinese: 该公司的竹内正树在接受BBC采访时表示：“我们的构想是将海面与深海垂直连接起来，我们相信通过这种方式，能够充分开发深海的潜在价值。”

sentences.english: Of course, there are engineering challenges in constructing an oceanic metropolis.
sentences.chinese: 当然，建造一座海洋大都市面临着诸多工程难题。

sentences.english: And living underwater would have major effects on the human body, especially as there is an increase in atmospheric pressure which could lead to the bends.
sentences.chinese: 而且水下生活也会对人体产生重大影响，尤其是水下气压的升高可能会导致潜水员患上减压病。

sentences.english: So, maybe it’s too soon to be packing our bags and setting up a new life three thousand metres under the sea!
sentences.chinese: 如此看来，现在就打包行李，去三千米深的海底开启新生活，或许还为时过早。
